title: So Many AI Models, How Do You Choose? The Leaderboard's #1 Isn't Always Right for You
description:
New models launch almost every week, and the leaderboard gets a new #1 right along with them — do you really need to switch every time? This video gives you a decision framework, for anyone building product features with tools or APIs like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

Using three questions — what the task is, how long you can wait, and how much you'll pay — the video walks you through choosing between a single flagship model, a cascade that starts cheap and escalates, or parallel cross-review where two models answer and a third judges. I run the actual numbers: under the same assumptions, a single flagship (Claude Opus 5.5) costs about $0.024 per request; the cascade (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite answers first) averages about $0.0096; and parallel cross-review (adding gpt-6-astra to answer alongside it, with Claude Sonnet 5 as judge) costs about $0.0944. Amounts are calculated from the official pricing pages' standard rates as of September 2026; the 30% escalation rate and the 3,000/600 input/output tokens are demo assumptions, not measured real-world traffic.

My take: a new #1 on the leaderboard every week shouldn't be your reason to switch models. Most work actually calls for the cheap-first, escalate-later cascade, and parallel cross-review should be reserved for decisions you really can't afford to get wrong. The full math, comparison tables, and the assumptions behind the latency reasoning are all in the article linked below.
